# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory (HTML viz; add --obsidian for a vault)
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## F-C1 decision: Codex session persistence vs resume

Decided from URI's requirements, not convenience:

* URI owns task/intent/execution state; the executor's thread/session id is **resumable execution metadata**. It is
  persisted only on the `attempt` row of the task that produced it (needed for safe continuation), never elsewhere.
* Reuse is bounded to one path: a `RESUME_SESSION` retry of the **same task**, under the **same authorization row**
  (admission re-checks validity, so a revoked or expired authorization blocks the resume), with the **same executor
  registration** (a re-registered executor runs fresh and the refusal is recorded as `attempt.resume_refused`), the
  **same model** (the model travels with the authorized work, never with the session), and a session id that still
  validates (`valid_session_id`, bypass tokens refused).
* Missing, stale or invalid session: Codex answers with a terminal error claim; reconciliation treats it as an ordinary
  failed attempt (`RETRY_FRESH` if budget remains, else `FAILED RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`). It can never produce
  COMPLETE and never bypasses the authority check: fail closed or the governed retry path.
* Settled/completed tasks are never re-admitted; a supervisor restart revokes the authority and fails the leftover
  (Phase 2B rule), so a resumable thread is abandoned after a restart (new ticket required).
* Codex thread persistence in the user's own Codex store: kept (no `--ephemeral`), because resume is a qualified
  capability (Phase 2C real evidence) and URI's correctness never depends on that store (failure = retry path). This is
  the product trade-off recorded in Phase 2C F-C1; the owner may still choose `--ephemeral` later (one spec change).

Tests: `tests/phase2d/test_session_resume.py` (normal continuation, cross-task reuse, re-registration, stale session
retry path, exhausted budget, revoked authority, expired window, completed task, bridge model/auth binding, restart).

## Qualification persistence and invalidation

A record is written only by a trusted qualification run (`phase2d_composition_qualification.py`) and only when the
direct probe succeeded AND the live auth status is ok. On every load (worker start, `harness_discover`) it is
re-validated; any drift invalidates it (reported, never silently inherited):

| Drift | Result |
|---|---|
| executable missing / different file at the path | `EXECUTABLE_MISSING` |
| executable bytes changed (npm `codex.CMD` shim included) | `EXECUTABLE_HASH_MISMATCH`; the bridge also pins the hash at run time (`EXECUTOR_BINARY_HASH_MISMATCH`, no task) |
| `--version` differs | `VERSION_MISMATCH` |
| record edited by hand | `RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH` (file unreadable / wrong schema: `RECORD_UNREADABLE` / `RECORD_SCHEMA`) |
| `FIXTURE_ONLY` record in a production profile | `LEVEL_NOT_ALLOWED` (only `--allow-fixture-qualification`, test profile) |
| provider refused/unknown (Antigravity) | `PROVIDER_REFUSED_OR_UNKNOWN` |
| model not in the record's `models` | bridge `NOT_STARTED:MODEL_NOT_QUALIFIED` before any task |
| authentication | never persisted; live probe each time (`AUTHENTICATED` / `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` / `AUTH_UNVERIFIED`), usable only when `AUTHENTICATED` |

Schema v2 (after independent review round 1; the v1 rows above remain and add to these):

| Drift / attack | Result |
|---|---|
| record edited and its digest recomputed | `RECORD_SIGNATURE_INVALID` (Ed25519 by the client key) |
| record copied from another client, or signed by another key | `RECORD_CLIENT_MISMATCH` / `RECORD_SIGNATURE_INVALID` |
| no trust anchor supplied by the composition | `NO_TRUST_ANCHOR` |
| record older than `expires_at` (default 30 days, max 90) | `RECORD_EXPIRED` |
| evidence missing, replaced, or about another provider/version/executable/model | `EVIDENCE_MISSING` / `EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH` / `EVIDENCE_CONTENT_MISMATCH` |
| payload behind an unchanged launcher shim replaced (node, codex.js, vendor binaries) | `LAUNCH_CHAIN_HASH_MISMATCH` at load; `NOT_STARTED:EXECUTOR_LAUNCH_CHAIN_MISMATCH` at run |
| a launcher name (e.g. `node`) now resolves elsewhere on the executor PATH | `LAUNCH_CHAIN_RESOLUTION_CHANGED` / `EXECUTOR_LAUNCH_CHAIN_MISMATCH` |
| native `.cmd/.bat/.ps1` launcher without a pinned chain | `LAUNCH_CHAIN_NOT_PINNED` |

Trust limit: the signing key is protected by current-user DPAPI (Phase 1 C1, same-user logical isolation). A process running
as the same Windows user can sign records; schema v2 defends against edits, copies, stale evidence and payload replacement,
not same-user malware. OS-loader DLLs outside the pinned directories and programs the executor spawns are not pinned.

Codex is **not** URI's permanent Main Brain: it is one qualified `(provider, executable, model)` row the server may
offer and the client may run; the deterministic row is always offered; click-to-choose selection is unchanged.

## UI / worker composition and the human approval path

* The UI remains outside authority: it sends `turn_start`, `turn_intent` (digest-bound confirm/abandon/select) and
  `turn_decide {turn_id, approve[, approval_digest]}`; it never sees tickets, keys or private state. A frame with a
  `ticket`, `reasoning` or `arguments` key is a schema violation.
* The worker binds the approval to its own pending record (turn, session, reasoning, approval request). With
  `approval_digest` the UI must echo the digest it displayed; a mismatch drops the pending turn (`APPROVAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH`).
* Changes after approval: the server ticket carries the argument/approval digests; the bridge re-verifies the arguments
  it will run (`ARGUMENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH`); the selection is bound at begin (`AUTHORITY_SELECTION_MISMATCH`).
* Cancellation: pre-dispatch `turn_cancel` (server `APPROVAL_DENIED`, nothing runs); post-dispatch `SupervisorBridge.cancel`
  (job kill, no re-admission, `execution_uncertain`); worker death propagates through the kill-on-close job.
  The single-threaded worker protocol exposes no mid-run cancel frame (NOT IMPLEMENTED, documented).
* Duplicate execution on reconnect/retry: pending state is memory-only (worker restart -> `TURN_NOT_PENDING`); a second
  live worker on the same client is refused by the frozen per-client mutex; the frozen server guards

  expires it (15 min idle / 60 min absolute); the user continues in a new session meanwhile.
* The frozen UI (`paired_runtime.dart`) is byte-identical and still spawns the frozen worker. Connecting it to the
  supervised worker needs either a UI change or a manifest/launcher change: both are cutover items (C7), not done.

composition that pairs it (persisted qualification -> Phase 1 registry + supervisor bindings -> bridge).

Server side. The frozen default composition lists exactly one row, the deterministic no-Brain source
(`uri_core.app.paired_server.default_composition`). Phase 2D does not change that file. Instead a Phase 2 server
profile reads an explicit policy file in the SERVER's own state root (`<state_root>/control/phase2_reasoning_policy.json`)
and lists its rows in addition to the deterministic one. A row is a (kind, provider, model) triple the owner chose to
offer; it is still only an *offer*: the client registry, the bridge and the ticket chain decide whether anything runs.
No row is ever inferred from an installed binary, a model advertisement or a client's claim.

Client side. `compose_client` (qualification.py) turns persisted, re-validated evidence into the Phase 1
`HarnessRegistry` qualification plus pinned `ExecutorBinding`s; `build_bridge` wires them into one `SupervisorBridge`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from uri_core.core.paired_reasoning import ReasoningSelectionPolicy

from .bridge import SupervisorBridge
from .qualification import ClientComposition, compose_client

POLICY_SCHEMA = "uri.phase2d.reasoning_policy.v1"
DETERMINISTIC_ROW = ("server_local_model", "uri-deterministic", None)
# The only kind Phase 2 adds rows for. Cloud-model and server-local-model rows stay owner decisions outside Phase 2.
ALLOWED_KINDS = ("client_external_harness",)
QUALIFIED_CAPABILITIES = ("remember_fact", "external_harness_task")
_PROVIDER = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$")
_MODEL = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,127}$")


class PolicyError(ValueError):
    pass


def policy_path(state_root) -> Path:
    return Path(state_root).resolve() / "control" / "phase2_reasoning_policy.json"


def load_policy_rows(path) -> frozenset:
    """Deterministic row + every valid row in the file. A malformed file is refused as a whole (fail closed: no
    harness rows), never partially accepted."""
    rows = {DETERMINISTIC_ROW}
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        return frozenset(rows)
    try:
        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        raise PolicyError("POLICY_UNREADABLE") from None
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema") != POLICY_SCHEMA or not isinstance(data.get("rows"), list):
        raise PolicyError("POLICY_SCHEMA")
    for row in data["rows"]:
        if not isinstance(row, dict) or set(row) != {"kind", "provider", "model"}:
            raise PolicyError("POLICY_ROW_SHAPE")
        kind, provider, model = row["kind"], row["provider"], row["model"]
        if kind not in ALLOWED_KINDS:
            raise PolicyError("POLICY_KIND_NOT_ALLOWED")
        if not isinstance(provider, str) or not _PROVIDER.fullmatch(provider):
            raise PolicyError("POLICY_PROVIDER_INVALID")
        if model is not None and (not isinstance(model, str) or not _MODEL.fullmatch(model)):
            raise PolicyError("POLICY_MODEL_INVALID")
        rows.add((kind, provider, model))
    return frozenset(rows)


def write_policy(path, rows) -> Path:
    """Owner-side helper: write an explicit policy file. `rows` are (kind, provider, model) triples."""
    p = Path(path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = sorted({tuple(r) for r in rows} - {DETERMINISTIC_ROW}, key=str)   # the deterministic row is implied, never listed
    body = {"schema": POLICY_SCHEMA, "rows": [{"kind": k, "provider": pr, "model": m} for k, pr, m in rows]}
    load_policy_rows_from_data(body)
    p.write_text(json.dumps(body, indent=1, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
    return p


def load_policy_rows_from_data(data):
    import tempfile
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f)
        name = f.name
    try:
        return load_policy_rows(name)
    finally:
        Path(name).unlink(missing_ok=True)


def phase2_server_composition(policy_file) -> dict:
    """`create_app(runtime, composition=...)` input for the Phase 2 server profile."""
    rows = load_policy_rows(policy_file)
    return {"policy": ReasoningSelectionPolicy(rows), "qualified": QUALIFIED_CAPABILITIES}


def build_bridge(client_root, composition: ClientComposition, **bridge_kwargs) -> SupervisorBridge:
    return SupervisorBridge(client_root, registry=composition.registry, executors=composition.executors, **bridge_kwargs)


def compose_and_build(client_root, *, trust, allow_fixture=False, auth_probe=None, environ=None, **bridge_kwargs):
    comp = compose_client(client_root, trust=trust, allow_fixture=allow_fixture, auth_probe=auth_probe, environ=environ)
    return comp, build_bridge(client_root, comp, **bridge_kwargs)

            entry = self.pending.pop(command["turn_id"], None)

        if kind == "turn_decide":

    identity; a bare tmp client root gets a test identity, stable for the life of the test process."""
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

    manifest = root / "client-manifest.json"

# URI Phase 2A: Durable Task Supervisor, architecture

Status: candidate, uncommitted, local only. Built on the frozen Phase 1 Core checkpoint
`final-closure-20261005-phase1.zip` (SHA-256 `31a34dcb...defeb98cf7`, base commit `e8e3b65`).
Nothing in `uri_core`, `uri_harness_adapters` or `uri_ui` was modified or imports the new package.

## Boundary

```
User intent -> URI Core (frozen, authority) -> [integration seam, NOT wired] -> uri_supervisor
                                                      |
        Durable Task -> Admission -> Fenced Attempt -> Effect Intent -> Effect/Evidence
                    -> Reconciliation -> Verified State -> Snapshot / Narration
```

`uri_supervisor` is a library. Core integration (approval verification before `submit_task`, UI routes) is
deliberately not done: it would require editing frozen files. The seam is `Supervisor.submit_task(...)`: the caller
must be Core code that already holds a confirmed, in-scope authorization. Phase 2A records and re-checks that scope
(op classes, executors, workspace, validity window) but cannot authenticate an approval itself.

## Modules

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `schema.py`, `ledger.py` | SQLite ledger, WAL + `synchronous=FULL`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions, append-only tables, invariant triggers, checked state transition, authority clock |
| `admission.py` | Resource pools, versioned executor registrations, atomic multi-claim admission, round-based aging, reservation, leases, circuit breakers |
| `supervisor.py` | Task intake, intent declaration, fenced spawn, stream recording, preemption, startup recovery, lease reaping, human decisions, re-examination |
| `recovery.py` | One reconciliation procedure for every attempt end (clean, crashed, interrupted) |
| `winproc.py` | Named kill-on-close Job Object per attempt, process identity (pid + creation time), identity-checked termination |
| `executors.py`, `stream.py` | Declarative executor specs (data), byte-level NDJSON splitter, declarative event rules |
| `postconditions.py` | URI-observed checks (file, hash, git, command, external reconciler, terminal success) and pre-attempt fingerprints |
| `snapshot.py`, `narration.py` | Bounded deterministic manager snapshot; evidence-grounded, mechanically verifiable narration |
| `crashpoints.py` | Inert-by-default deterministic crash injection used by the qualification tests |

## Task states

`QUEUED` (pre-admission, needed for the queue) then `RUNNING`, `RECOVERING`, and one of `COMPLETE`, `RETRY_SAFE`,
`UNCERTAIN`, `FAILED`, `NEEDS_USER`. `RETRY_SAFE` re-enters admission. Detailed reasons live in `reason_code`,
`recovery_decision` and `uncertainty` rows, not in the state vocabulary. `RESUME` is a decision action, `COMPENSATE` is
an effect, neither is a state.

|---|---|---|
| QUEUED | RUNNING | atomic admission (attempt, admission, claims, fence) |
| RUNNING | RECOVERING | attempt fenced |
